text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- The Portuguese government is considering the possibility of abolishing the property transfer tax "sisa" and replacing it with value added tax (VAT.)

- The Portuguese oppose abortion, according to a poll. When asked "In the absence of medical reasons, should abortion be free?", a question proposed by the opposition Social Democratic Party (PSD) for a referendum, 52.5 percent of those questioned replied "No."
- Police general Gabriel Teixeira will submit proposals to the interior ministry today to boost discipline within the police force.
- Economy Minister Augusto Mateus told reporters he believed that unemployment in Portugal would not rise in 1997.

- President Jorge Sampaio was invited to attend the swearing-in ceremony of the new Angolan government of national reconciliation in Luanda, set for January 25, a diplomatic source told the paper. The presidency has not yet replied to the invitation.
